summary: The study describes the formation of multitwinned Zn2TiO4 nanowires through a solid-state reaction of ZnO nanowires with a conformal TiO2 shell deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD). The process involves the oriented attachment of preformed spinel nanobricks and Ostwald ripening. The reaction temperature, shell thickness, and annealing conditions significantly influence the formation of multitwinned structures.
evidence: The formation of multitwinned Zn2TiO4 nanowires was achieved by annealing ZnO nanowires with a TiO2 shell at 900 °C. The process involves the oriented attachment of preformed spinel nanobricks and Ostwald ripening. The study also highlights the role of the TiO2 shell thickness and reaction temperature in the formation of multitwinning.
